A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CBGBench. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial additions and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecular-generation and lead-optimization experiments, receptor case studies, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 3-8 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds MolCraft and VoxBind comparisons, extended case-study results, and molecule-size/LBE statistics in Table 11.

M1.justification: No substantive change is specified to the proposed graph-completion framework, modular task adaptations or molecular reconstruction procedure. MolCraft and VoxBind expand the evaluated methods rather than introduce a new CBGBench algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use CrossDocked2020 for de novo generation and the same four lead-optimization tasks, plus ADRB1/DRD3 case studies and GEOM-DRUG controls. Binding MOAD appears in v3's review of prior DiffSBDD experiments, not as a newly evaluated CBGBench dataset.

E2.justification: v3 adds MolCraft and VoxBind to the de novo comparisons, and MolCraft to all four lead-optimization comparisons and the ADRB1 plots. Existing comparators remain. Although v3's case-study text says eight methods were tested on both receptors, the DRD3 figure still displays the original seven.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes the stated GEOM-DRUG control sample from 200 to 100 molecules, retaining 200 actives per target. The new LBE analysis uses five atom-count bins. Core dataset splits and generation counts remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 and Table 11 add an analysis of whether extremely small molecules undermine LBE, reporting molecule frequencies and efficacy by size bin. This supplements the existing size-energy correlation plots, which are retained from v2.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies training-seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or reported significance tests. Aggregate rankings and sample-distribution plots retain the same reporting practice; the added comparisons do not introduce run-level uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive MolCraft/VoxBind results and changes the reported overall winner from TargetDiff to MolCraft. Shared raw scores in Tables 3-6 remain unchanged, while ranks change. Table 8 adds MolCraft results and changes GraphBP's side-chain Vina Score from -5.01 to 5.01. New LBE size-bin results and ADRB1 findings further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The graph-completion definitions and LBE/MPBG formulas are retained. The edge-set symbol correction is notational. Appendix B.4 adds a physical rationale for existing LBE normalization, without a substantive new formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and five-task contributions remain intact. The abstract no longer explicitly claims to provide pretrained model versions, emphasizing the unified pipeline instead. The introduction also qualifies lead-optimization generalization by explicitly highlighting substantial remaining room for improvement.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting CNN performance to many-body perception and interprets mostly negative MPBG values as inadequate lead optimization. Appendix B.4 substantially expands the interpretation of LBE through pocket-size preferences, ligand strain and rare extreme-size samples. These extend v2's shorter mechanism discussions and size-energy observations.

D1.justification: New Appendix D and Table 13 document software and hardware, per-method batch sizes, network dimensions and depths, optimizers, learning rates, sampling steps and configuration location. They also disclose checkpoint provenance. v2 mainly referred to default configurations and iteration budgets; this is a substantial reproducibility disclosure, not evidence of changed retained implementations.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and new Appendix A expand the methodological history, while Table 12 compares prior evaluation coverage. Added literature covers MolCraft, Bayesian flow networks, ligand-efficiency criticism and optimization approaches. VoxBind and VoxMol were already cited in v2 but receive substantially expanded treatment in v3.

P1.justification: The compact taxonomy gains a substantial method-by-method chronological exposition. The abstract and graph-completion explanation are revised, and appendices are reorganized around methodological review, evaluation, codebase, implementation and results. This substantially expands the explanatory structure while retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v3 adds the graph-completion schematic and four tables covering method history, LBE by size, prior evaluation coverage and hyperparameters. It expands comparison tables, transposes the functional-group results table, and rearranges and extends ADRB1 plots. The document template and layout also change; several existing diagrams are simply relocated.

improvement.justification: The added comparators, implementation details and LBE analysis provide useful breadth and transparency. However, v2's Table 7 ranks follow its weighted totals, whereas v3 ranks VoxBind fifth despite its displayed total of 8.25 exceeding second-ranked TargetDiff's 7.71. The added VoxBind atom proportions in Table 14 also sum to 1.738. These new inconsistencies undermine central comparative evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment against the benefits of the expansion.
